svg.title: Unlimited envelopes at 0 dB SNR
svg.desc: Whole-band RMS envelope against the narrow-band magnitude at the pitch over the Decoder's slot window, with and without noise at 0 dB SNR.
svg.text: Why the receiver listens in a narrow band around the pitch: 0 dB SNR
hf transmission of “Hi” + AWGN at 0 dB (key-down tone in 2500 Hz), USB receiver 300–2700 Hz, 150 ms of silence before it.
Both envelopes average over the Decoder's slot window, 0.75 T = 12 ms (83 Hz of noise bandwidth at the pitch); 1.0 = the crest A.
narrow band (83 Hz) at the pitch, 1500 Hz: magnitude
In 2400 Hz the noise is as strong as the tone; in the 83 Hz slot window it is 14.6 dB weaker (2400/83).
The receiver first finds the pitch (the tune tone), then mixes it to 0 Hz and measures every slot over 0.75 T: never one wideband envelope.
